profile.headline: Scientific Software Engineer
profile.summary: Software engineer with a background in mechanical engineering and experience in application development for visualization and analysis for NASA space missions. Passionate about learning, collaboration, and working smarter.

positions.title: Scientific Software Engineer
positions.description:
•	Developed an application-building infrastructure in Java that allows combinations of trajectory comparison, instrument planning, requirement validation, and data download, processing, and analysis. Framework supports NASA space missions and instruments such as: EIS, MISE, and REASON on Europa Clipper; Mini-RF on the Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter; and MIMI on Cassini-Huygens, among others. 
•	Designed and expanded APIs that are used across various projects. APIs include: interactive visualization of large-scale (50+ GB) images with overlays; quasi-3D renderings of planetary bodies and data; interactive and customizable data visualization and plotting.
•	Participated in various internal instrument proposals from building computer aided design (CAD) models to creating automated calibration tests in Python. Coordinated with international partners to integrate components such as optical assemblies and calibration targets. 
•	Restructured group version control setup by integrating Maven, Git, and GitLab with several virtual machines to provide automated updating, testing, and deploying capabilities, which increased collaboration and improved user workflow efficiency.

company.name: The Johns Hopkins University Applied Physics Laboratory

positions.title: Residential Advisor
positions.description:
• Supervised and mentored 25-50 residents each year while upholding university standards and regulations.
• Developed and coordinated programming, established a sense of community, and resolved a range of issues.
• Completed 200+ hours of training in areas including leadership, conflict resolution, and diversity awareness.

positions.title: NASA Summer Intern
positions.description:
• Developed program to communicate with various types of hardware. Integrated program and hardware with an infrared camera to create an automated and efficient instrument for capturing thermal images.
• Constructed an electro-mechanical system to thermally control and evaluate a blackbody shutter. Processed and analyzed data, then presented the system’s limitations and possible improvements.
• Coordinated with vendors to budget and design custom components for a proposed planetary hyperspectral imager. Designed CAD model assembly of the imager.

company.name: The Johns Hopkins University Applied Physics Laboratory

positions.title: Mechanical Engineering Intern
positions.description:
Utilized CAD and finite element analysis (FEA) software (StressCheck) along with VBA to:
• Analyze the crack growth of an F-35 bulkhead. Created automated driver compatible with any StressCheck model, producing efficiency and versatility for future use. Presented results to company’s leadership.
• Simulate several mechanical treatments. Designed program to optimize efficiency and be accessible to clients without StressCheck experience.
•Enter NAFEMS Benchmark Challenge. Developed program to determine the collapse load of a custom steel plate. Presented results to NAFEMS to demonstrate StressCheck’s modeling accuracy.

positions.title: Student Researcher
positions.description: Researched Australian sustainable technologies and their socioeconomic impact. Created and presented report with in-depth comparison and analysis of available energy sources and related outside factors.

positions.title: Intern
positions.description:
Aided chief architect on and offsite. Recorded data, designed CAD models, and assisted by analyzing projects and developing ideas. Gained experience with project management and creative collaboration.

http://www.jnealdesign.com

volunteerExperiences.description: Developed and taught curriculums with a focus on healthy habits and nutrition for inner-city kids through an after school program.
